speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a psychiatric condition and a new onset movement disorder; can you describe exactly how your movements have changed and when you first noticed the symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That's great to hear your psychiatric symptoms are improving. Since you started risperidone two months ago, have you noticed any stiffness, tremors, or shaking movements since then? Also, are these movements constant or do they disappear when you are relaxed?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Risperidone-Induced Akathisia.

Based on your description of an inability to remain still, persistent restlessness, and repetitive pacing, this clinical picture strongly suggests akathisia, a common extrapyramidal side effect of antipsychotic medications like risperidone. Given the timing since you started the medication two months ago, this is the most likely explanation for your new movement disorder. We can manage this by adjusting your medication dose or adding a specific medication to counteract the side effects.
